title: Lists and Objects in Thunkable — Review Quiz

questions.question: What is the index of "Fish" in the list [Cat, Dog, Fish, Bird, Turtle]?
You use the block: `in list, get # 5`. What value is returned from the list [Cat, Dog, Fish, Bird, Turtle]?
You use the block: `in list, set # 1 as "Hamster"`. What does the list [Cat, Dog, Fish, Bird, Turtle] look like now?
You use the block: `in list [Cat, Dog, Fish, Bird, Turtle], insert at last as "Snake"`. How many items are in the list now, and what is at index 6?
You use the block: `in list, remove # 1` on the list [Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday]. What does the list look like now?
Starting from the list [Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday], you use: `in list, remove # 3`. What value is now at index 3?
Starting from the list [Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday], you use: `in list, set # 4 as "Friday"`. What value is at index 4?
Starting from the list [Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday], you first use `in list, remove # 2` and then use `in list, get # 2`. What value is returned?
A list in Thunkable contains the values: 42, "hello", true. Is this allowed?
answers: No — a list can only hold numbers
No — a list can only hold text
Yes — a list can contain multiple different data types at once
Yes — but only if the list has exactly 3 items

questions.question: When you add a new item to a list in Thunkable, does the list automatically sort itself?
answers: No, lists are not organized by default
Yes, it sorts by the order you added items, newest first

questions.question: How do you access the value "Soccer" from an object with keys: name=Maya, sport=Soccer, age=16, team=Eagles?
You use the block: `set property "team" of object to "Wolves"` an object with keys: name=Maya, sport=Soccer, age=16, team=Eagles. What is the value of the "team" key now?
You use the block: `get property "age" of object` on an object with keys: name=Maya, sport=Soccer, age=16, team=Eagles. What value is returned?
You want to add a new piece of information to this object: the player's jersey number is 7. What do you need to provide?
answers: An index number and a value
A key and a value (a key-value pair)

questions.question: What is the main difference between how lists and objects organize their data?
answers: Lists use named keys; objects use numbered indexes
Lists use numbered indexes; objects use named keys
Lists can only hold text; objects can hold any type
Objects can hold more items than lists

questions.question: You create an object with the fields: brand = "Nike", size = 10, color = "Red". You use the block: `get property "brand" of object`. What is returned?
You are building an app that keeps a to-do list of tasks (e.g., "Buy milk", "Call mom", "Study for test"). Which data structure is the best choice?
answers: Object — because each task needs a named key
List — because it is a collection of similar items
Object — because tasks are related to each other
Neither — use a separate variable for each task

questions.question: You are building an app that stores a single restaurant's details: name, address, phone number, and cuisine type. Which data structure is the best choice?
answers: List — because it can store multiple values
Object — because the data is related and each piece has a descriptive label
List — because restaurant data is unordered
Object — because objects are always better than lists

questions.question: You are building a music player app and need to store a queue of song titles that will play in order. Which data structure is the best choice?
answers: List — because it is an ordered collection of similar values
Object — because the queue needs named keys

questions.question: You are building a weather app and need to store today's forecast data: temperature, humidity, wind speed, and condition (e.g., "Sunny"). Which data structure is the best choice?
answers: List — because you can use indexes to access each value
List — because weather data is simple
Object — because each piece of data has a clear label and they are all related
Object — because objects are faster than lists
